raw_case_text:
A 39-year-old single Saudi Arabian man with no prior medical history presented to our emergency department complaining of a reddish mass in his left eye that had been slowly growing over the past 6 months. He had no other ocular symptoms, such as pain, photophobia, or visual changes, but did report experiencing a weight loss of 12 kg in 9 months preceding the assessment date. The patient's medical and ocular history was unremarkable, with no chronic medication use and no previous history of trauma. Regarding social history, the patient did not report engaging in sexual activity, illegal drug use, or having a prior blood transfusion.
The patient's height and weight at admission were 169 cm and 88 kg, respectively. Physical examination of the patient confirmed that there were no lesions in the oral cavity, mucocutaneous changes, or lymphadenopathy. Ophthalmologically, the patient had full extra-ocular range of motion, the best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes, pupil examination was normal, and intraocular pressure was 14 mm Hg and 19 mm Hg in the right and left eyes, respectively. On slit-lamp examination, a large, diffuse, elevated, dark-reddish fleshy mass was visualized over the left bulbar conjunctiva, along with areas of subconjunctival hemorrhage sparing the superior bulbar and palpebral conjunctiva (shown in Fig. 1). The lesion was loosely connected to the underlying tissue. Examination of the right eye and fundoscopic examination of both eyes were normal.
Owing to the large size of the mass, an incisional biopsy was first performed as both a diagnostic and therapeutic (debulking) procedure. A 5 mm x 2 mm mass was excised from the inferior bulbar conjunctival lesion, and bleeding vessels were obstructed by cauterization. Given that the tumor site was approaching the inferior fornix, an amniotic membrane graft was used to close the area of excision to decrease the risk of scarring, fibrosis, and symblepharon formation. Subsequently, a bandage contact lens was applied. There were no intra- or postoperative complications.
Histopathological examination of the biopsied tissue revealed proliferation of spindle-shaped endothelial cells, slit-like formations, and numerous extravasated red blood cells and inflammatory cells, consistent with KS (shown in Fig. 2). Immunohistochemical staining (shown in Fig. 3) strongly supported the diagnosis of KS.
Serologic and immunologic tests upon admission confirmed HIV infection, with a viral load of 186,876 copies/mL, and the patient's CD4+ T lymphocyte count was 169 cells/mm3. Oncology and infectious disease consultation data were also obtained. There was no evidence of nodular or distal metastases on whole-body positron emission tomography imaging.
Subsequently, owing to the local presentation and significant lesion extension noted in this case, highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) was initiated along with local irradiation of the tumor. The patient received radiotherapy at a dose of 20 Gy over 10 fractions. All fractions were delivered within 10 days. The lesion resolved completely in response to the local irradiation, and only mild redness, without any fibrosis or ocular range of motion restrictions, was observed at the 8-month follow-up (shown in Fig. 4). Multidisciplinary follow-ups were scheduled for the patient, who has had favorable responses with no relapses till the time of the last follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old single Saudi Arabian man presented to the emergency department with a 6-month history of a slowly enlarging reddish mass in his left eye.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 6 months prior to presentation, the patient noticed a painless, progressively growing reddish mass on the surface of his left eye. He also reported an unintentional 12 kg weight loss over the preceding 9 months.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical and ocular history; no prior trauma or blood transfusions. Denied sexual activity or illicit drug use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 12 kg weight loss over 9 months; negative for ocular pain, photophobia, or visual acuity changes. No chronic medications.

objective.physical_examination: Height 169 cm, weight 88 kg. General physical examination showed no oral cavity lesions, mucocutaneous lesions, or peripheral lymphadenopathy. Ophthalmic examination revealed best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20 bilaterally, full extraocular motility, normal pupillary reflexes, intraocular pressure of 14 mmHg (right eye) and 19 mmHg (left eye), and normal bilateral fundoscopy. Slit-lamp examination of the left eye revealed a large, diffuse, elevated, dark-reddish fleshy mass over the inferior bulbar conjunctiva approaching the inferior fornix, with surrounding subconjunctival hemorrhage sparing the superior bulbar and palpebral conjunctiva; the right eye was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 169 cells/mm3. Incisional debulking biopsy (5 x 2 mm) of the left inferior bulbar conjunctival mass with amniotic membrane graft reconstruction and bandage contact lens placement was performed; histopathology and immunohistochemistry demonstrated spindle-shaped endothelial cell proliferation, slit-like vascular spaces, extravasated erythrocytes, and inflammatory infiltrate diagnostic of Kaposi sarcoma. Whole-body PET imaging showed no nodal or distant metastases.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary isolated bulbar conjunctival Kaposi sarcoma as the initial presenting manifestation of advanced HIV/AIDS, confirmed by conjunctival biopsy histopathology/immunohistochemistry, positive HIV serology, plasma HIV viral load of 186,876 copies/mL, and CD4+ T-cell count of 169 cells/mm3. Following multidisciplinary oncology and infectious disease consultation, the patient was treated with Surgical debulking/amniotic membrane grafting, initiation of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), and local external-beam radiotherapy (20 Gy delivered in 10 fractions over 10 days). At 8-month follow-up, the conjunctival lesion had completely resolved with only mild residual hyperemia, intact ocular motility, and no local recurrence or systemic metastasis.
